Subject: Quick post-demo recap + DPA clarifications

Hi Ana —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so your team can move to legal review: 

- Scope: You indicated Luma Health will act as the controller for PII submitted by patients and Redwood would be the processor for inference and telemetry. Please confirm if that remains the expectation for the signed DPA (controller = Luma, processor = Redwood).
- Breach notification: You referenced an internal target of "as soon as possible" — can you confirm whether Luma needs an initial notification within 72 hours or 24 hours for any suspected subprocessor incident?
- Retention: Luma asked about PII retention windows and logs. What are your target retention windows for patient-identifiable inputs (months) and for request/trace logs used for troubleshooting (days)?
- Subprocessors: I'll attach our current subprocessor list and SOC2 summary. Can you flag any allowed/blocked subprocessor categories (e.g., monitoring, hosted DB, observability)?

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v2_redline.pdf (redline we discussed), SOC2-Summary.pdf

Next steps: If you can reply with the controller confirmation, target breach-notify window, and retention targets, I’ll loop in Legal to propose exact language or call out any non-starters. Happy to schedule a short call if helpful.

Best,

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | (415) 555-0172

From: Ana Torres <ana.torres@lumahc.com>

Cc: DevOps Team <security@lumahc.com>
Date: 2028-09-14T14:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick post-demo recap + DPA clarifications

Thanks Jordan — great demo. Answers below: 

- Controller/processor: Confirmed — Luma will be the controller. We need contract language that reflects that data submitted by our patients is under our direction.
- Breach notification: For incidents involving patient-identifiable data we require an initial notification within 72 hours of Luma becoming aware of the incident; followed by a fuller incident report within 14 days. For subprocessor incidents that don’t materially affect patient data, we expect notification within 5 business days.
- Retention: Our baseline ask is 13 months for patient-identifiable records that the application stores for business purposes. For request/trace logs used for debugging/triage we’re aiming for 90 days. If you have configurable retention options (30/90/365) that would be ideal.
- Subprocessors: We need a named list (or categories) of subprocessors and an onboarding notification process for any new subprocessor that will handle PII. Please include encryption at rest and access controls in the response.

Can you have legal provide a redline or comment pass on the attached DPA? Also please send the subprocessor list and SOC2 attestation. Thanks!

—Ana
Ana Torres
Head of Integrations | Luma Health

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: jordan.blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Quick post-demo recap + DPA clarifications

Hi Ana —

Thanks for the clear summary and for flagging the retention/logging targets. I reviewed Jordan’s redline and the attached SOC2 summary; below are our commitments and proposed contract language to address your items. Happy to set a short call to walk through these.

1) Controller / Processor: We will accept language that recognizes Luma Health as Controller and Redwood Inference as Processor. We will include the standard data processing clauses to reflect that relationship.

2) Breach notification: Redwood can commit to an "initial notification" to the customer within 72 hours of Redwood becoming aware of an incident affecting customer patient data. We will follow with a substantive incident report within 14 calendar days. For incidents limited to a subprocessor that do not materially impact patient data, we propose a 5 business day notification window. Suggested contract text can be found in the attached redline (Redwood_DPA_v2_redline.pdf); see Section 6(a).

3) Retention: Our platform supports configurable retention profiles. Default request/trace logs retention is 30 days; we can offer a 90-day retention profile for enterprise agreements at no incremental license cost for this pilot. For patient-identifiable inputs that Luma directs Redwood to persist, we can set a 13-month retention window as requested. We will include retention control language and a process for deletion on termination.

4) Subprocessors & encryption: Attached is a sanitized subprocessor roster (we will provide a live, full roster via a secure link once the NDA/DPA is in place). High-level: cloud infra provider (primary compute), managed database provider, observability/monitoring vendor, and a small number of ML ops vendors. All subprocessors who have access to PII are required to maintain encryption at rest and role-based access controls; we will include a certification clause in the DPA. We will also add a 30-day notice requirement for new subprocessors that will process PII, with an exception process if immediate onboarding is required.

Attachments included here: Redwood_DPA_v2_redline.pdf (redline with suggested language), SOC2-Summary.pdf, playbook_dpa_mapping.xlsx.

Next steps: Jordan — please review the redline Section 6 and confirm you’re comfortable sending this back to Ana. Ana — if that aligns, we can schedule a 30-minute legal-to-legal call later this week to go through the redline and subprocessor link.

Best regards,

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
